geometry_edits.rationale: Recast the dominant form as a more section-driven mass so the program can express active ground and upper hierarchy rather than a generic cantilevered box.
Use a folded section family to create a clearer roof/section profile and improve programmatic distinction between ground and upper mass.
Orient the section logic to preserve a compact neighborhood block and keep the public threshold readable on the frontage side.
Introduce a true courtyard void as a nested public-space organizer inside the dominant mass.
Keep the void substantial enough to be usable while preserving a strong surrounding mass.
Open the courtyard toward the verified access edge to satisfy the active public threshold requirement.
Make the courtyard the new organizing root so the original mass remains in ancestry while the public void becomes primary.

graph_edits.rationale: Shift the dominant mass from a pure cantilevered block to a carved ground-oriented figure that can support the required public threshold.
Reduce the aggressiveness of the overhang so the mass reads as a calmer neighborhood block with more legible base condition.
Add a bounded entry notch tied to the public access edge to create an explicit ground-level threshold and court-like arrival space.
Align the notch to the program-frame access side so the ground response engages the verified frontage.
Keep the opening bounded rather than turning the whole object into a void.
Make the ground incision legible without destroying the dominant mass.

rationale: The candidate reads as a compact single dominant mass, but the visible form is still mostly a rectilinear block with limited spatial generosity. Across the four views it is coherent, though the silhouette is only mildly articulated and not strongly capacity-bearing. The main problem is program fit: the neighborhood-living brief asks for an active ground threshold and a clear public void or terrace, yet the blue frontage edge is answered only weakly, with no strong carved court or legible entry seam on the access side. The top and oblique views suggest a simple lifted/canted chunk rather than a mass that clearly organizes public ground and upper hierarchy. Repair integrity is acceptable because the object remains one piece and does not visibly self-intersect, but the current book-like clipping/reflect language feels abstracted and underexpressed for the stated semantics. The references support courtyard/public-threshold thinking; the candidate currently falls short of that principle.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Compact commercial massing organized around a legible central void/court and an active edge condition.
Courtyard-centered neighborhood-scale public space with a strong indoor-outdoor threshold.
Simple grounded frontage with clear occupied edge and restrained upper enclosure.
